messages.subject: sam() using different sub-samples
parts:
I have question please. I have a sample of 156 students who answered at least one of two surveys. 136 students responded to personality related questions 110 to Lifelong learning related and only 87 to both. I'm primarily interested in the relationship among latent variables. Is there any way to use global sam estimating the measurement model parameters on different samples, i.e. the personality measurement model on 136 , LLL on 109 and the latents on the 87? Not quite sure how to proceed and how to take into account the different uncertainties associated. Many thanks in advance. 

 Measurement models fitted - separately for largest sub-samples possible, then:

# Assembling the Lambda (factor loadings in measurement models) and Theta (var-cov matrix of instrument residual errors) matrices
Lambda <- lav_matrix_bdiag(lavInspect(fit_C, "est")$lambda,
                           lavInspect(fit_O, "est")$lambda,
                           lavInspect(fit_LLS, "est")$lambda)
Theta <- lav_matrix_bdiag(lavInspect(fit_C, "est")$theta,
                          lavInspect(fit_O, "est")$theta,
                          lavInspect(fit_LLS, "est")$theta)

# biased sample variance-covariance matrix
N <- nrow(df)
S <- cov(df) * (N - 1L)/N
....

Not sure if I understood what you want nor why.
Wouldn’t it be better to simply do a single model with missing="pairwise"?

Best,
Yago
